doc: What each finding of timeline-disl-fbl that was known only by reading looks like when its fixture is read or edited through the vendored example binding (src/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl.Tests/Conformance/timeline.fbl) and compared with what Parity/timeline.transcript.json records today's code doing. Checked by Parity/TimelineFindings.Tests.cs: an unlisted difference fails, and so does a listed one that has changed or no longer occurs. Never edit the vendored binding, a fixture written before its test, or an assertion instead.

findings.observed: set qvperiod timeline.row = "3": the transcript writes @8 -1 +"    row: 3\r\n"; the binding writes @8 -1 +"    row: \"3\"\r\n"
findings.reason: Finding B5, what is left of it once every edit is written through the module's binding (timeline-disl-fbl task 6): a label, a begin, an end and a relation's label are now written as the example binding writes them, in their own span and style with a trailing comment kept, and a value set to what it holds writes nothing. A row written quoted is not: the module's binding reads row as text (finding B13), and the library writes an int given to a slot read as text plain, where the example binding, which types the row, keeps the quotes. The tool wrote it plain before too.

findings.observed: the transcript records no finding; the binding reports fbl.header-mismatch at line 1: The body does not carry the binding's header mark ('timeline: 1'); it is read anyway.
findings.reason: Finding B9. The tool reads a document without the timeline: 1 marker, or with another version, and reports nothing; the example binding's header reports fbl.header-mismatch. The module's binding declares no header (Q2's default: switched off in this conversion).

findings.observed: the transcript records line 6 | Error | timeline.unparseable | This is not YAML that can be read: Duplicate key label; the binding reads 2 elements and reports fbl.duplicate-key at line 6: The key 'label' appears again in this mapping; only the first is read.
findings.reason: Finding B10. YamlDotNet refuses a mapping with a key written twice, so the tool reports the file as timeline.unparseable and opens nothing; FBL 7.4 reads the body, binds the first key and reports fbl.duplicate-key as a warning. The module keeps TimelineYamlSyntax as the stand-in that refuses such a file as today (Requirement 4.2, Amendment 1); the finding is not forwarded (Q2).

findings.observed: esmapping: the transcript a moment, the binding a period | essequence: the transcript a moment, the binding a period
findings.reason: Finding B11. The tool reads an entry as a period only when its end key holds a scalar (the empty one and null included); when end holds a mapping or a sequence it is a moment. The binding's has(entry.end) is true for every end key, so those two are periods. An empty end: and end: null agree. Definition defect: the module's binding states the tool's rule, or the difference is ruled on.

findings.observed: rowfloat: the transcript row 0, the binding 1 | rowhex: the transcript row 0, the binding 16 | rowoctal: the transcript row 0, the binding 15 | rowexponent: the transcript row 0, the binding 10
findings.reason: Finding B13. The tool reads a row with .NET's integer parse of the scalar's text, so 1.0, 0x10, 0o17 and 1e1 are row 0; the example binding converts the typed value, so they are rows 1, 16, 15 and 10. "3" and +4 agree. Definition defect: the module's binding reads row as text, without quoted and fallback, and the row is parsed as the tool parses it.

findings.observed: nbperiod: the transcript begin "", the binding unset | nbmoment: the transcript begin "", the binding unset
findings.reason: Finding B14. The tool reads a missing begin as the empty text and reports it as an unreadable time; the binding leaves the attribute unset, which a rule that reads it as null does not report. Definition defect: the module's binding gives begin default "".

findings.observed:
execute timeline.add-moment on new:1767312000,4: the transcript writes @30 -0 +"    -   id: minted-6
        label: New moment
        begin: 2026-01-02
        row: 4
"; the binding writes @10 -0 +"    -   id: minted-6
        label: New moment
        begin: 2026-01-02
        row: 4
"
findings.reason: Found by B7's fixture, not in the requirements. The tool appends a new element after the last entry of elements; the example binding's insert.place is after-last, which FBL defines as right after the last entry of the same rule, so once the last entry is a period a new moment goes after the last moment, in the middle of the list. Definition defect: the module's binding writes place end for both element rules.
